question: What's the APY on 1st Rate Checking right now?
expected_answer: 1st Rate Checking pays 2.50% APY (2.47% dividend rate) on balances of $5,000-$24,999.99; balances of $25,000+ earn 0.10% and under $5,000 earn 0.00% (rates effective 06/02/2026).
note: S05 rates-59a9e6.md and personal-checking-accounts-b29d89.md: $5k-$24,999.99 tier 2.47%/2.50% eff 06/02/2026. Stale: checking-offer-lp, tax-checking-offer-lp and newcard-balancetransfer-lp in S05 still show 2.96%/3.00% APY 'up to 3.00%' (eff 07/01/2025); S01/S02 /rates also showed 3.00% (eff 03/03/2026). Rates page > LP and newer-dated wins.

question: how much interest do u get on 1st rate checking if i keep like 10k in it
expected_answer: A $10,000 balance falls in the $5,000-$24,999.99 tier, which earns 2.50% APY (2.47% dividend rate), effective 06/02/2026.
note: Paraphrase of dep-01. S05 rates-59a9e6.md / personal-checking-accounts-b29d89.md. Landing pages (checking-offer-lp, tax-checking-offer-lp, newcard-balancetransfer-lp) still show the old 2.96%/3.00% tier (eff 07/01/2025).

question: I've got about $30,000 sitting in my 1st Rate Checking. What APY am I actually earning on that?
expected_answer: 0.10% APY. Once the balance is above $25,000 the whole balance earns the lower rate: $25,000-$99,999.99 earns 0.10% (the 2.50% APY applies only to balances of $5,000-$24,999.99).
note: S05 rates-59a9e6.md 1st Rate tiers: $25k-$99,999.99 0.10%/0.10%; checking-offer-lp text: 'If your balance goes above $25,000, your entire balance will earn the lower rate'. A sloppy answer quotes the 2.50% headline tier (allowed only as context). 3.00% is the stale LP value.

question: As of the end of May 2026, what was the top APY on Dupaco's 1st Rate Checking?
expected_answer: 3.00% APY (2.96% dividend rate) on balances of $5,000-$24,999.99, per rates effective 03/03/2026.
note: Ground truth = S02 (2026-05-19). S02 rates-59a9e6.md 1st Rate table: $5k-$24,999.99 2.96%/3.00%, eff 03/03/2026. S03 onward shows 2.47%/2.50% eff 06/02/2026 (after the as_of date), so 2.50% is wrong for this date. Avoid dates 06/02-06/08 (rate change effective before the S03 crawl).

question: what is the 12 month certificate rate
expected_answer: The regular 12-month term-share certificate pays 3.40% APY (3.37% dividend rate), $1,000 minimum, effective 06/02/2026.
note: S05 rates-59a9e6.md Regular Certificates: 12 Month 3.37%/3.40%. In S01/S02 the 12-month was 2.88%/2.90% (eff 03/03/2026); changed in S03 (eff 06/02/2026). business-rates shows the same 3.40% for business certificates. 2.90% in S05 only appears as the Visa balance-transfer APR, irrelevant here.

question: What was the APY on a 12-month CD at Dupaco around May 25, 2026?
expected_answer: 2.90% APY (2.88% dividend rate) on the regular 12-month certificate, $1,000 minimum (rates effective 03/03/2026).
note: Ground truth = S02 (2026-05-19) rates-59a9e6.md: 12 Month 2.88%/2.90%. S03+ show 3.37%/3.40% eff 06/02/2026 (after as_of). 3.40% not put in must_not because the 6-month term also paid 3.40% then and could be mentioned legitimately.

question: What did the 17-month certificate special pay as of July 1, 2026?
expected_answer: The 17 Month Fixed Certificate Special paid 3.85% APY (3.81% dividend, $1,000 minimum); the 17 Month Fixed Jumbo Special paid 3.95% APY (3.91% dividend, $100,000 minimum), rates effective 06/02/2026.
note: Ground truth = S03 (2026-06-09) rates-59a9e6.md Special: 17M 3.81%/3.85%, 17M jumbo 3.91%/3.95%, eff 06/02/2026. Later: S04 3.95%/4.05% (eff 07/14/2026), S05 4.10%/4.20% (eff 09/01/2026). 17-month special did not exist in S01/S02 (25-month special instead).

question: Which certificate specials was Dupaco running in mid-May 2026 and at what rates?
expected_answer: Four specials (rates effective 03/03/2026): 10 Month Fixed Special 3.80% APY ($1,000 min), 10 Month Fixed Jumbo Special 3.90% APY ($100,000 min), 25 Month Fixed Special 3.60% APY ($1,000 min), 25 Month Fixed Jumbo Special 3.70% APY ($100,000 min).
note: Ground truth = S01 (2026-05-12) rates-59a9e6.md Special table. The 25-month specials vanished in S03 (replaced by 17-month). Current S05 specials (17M 4.10/4.20, 10M 3.90/4.00) are wrong for this date.

question: What's the Roth IRA 17 month special paying these days?
expected_answer: Roth: 17 Month Fixed Special pays 4.10% APY (4.06% dividend, $1,000 minimum); the Roth 17 Month Fixed Jumbo Special pays 4.20% APY (4.15% dividend, $100,000 minimum). Effective 09/01/2026.
note: S05 rates-59a9e6.md Special IRAs and personal-retirement-e090f4.md agree (eff 09/01/2026). Stale: S03 3.85%/3.95% (eff 06/02/2026), S04 3.95%/4.05% (eff 07/14/2026).

question: traditional ira 17mo special rate?
expected_answer: Traditional: 17 Month Fixed Special is 4.10% APY (4.06% dividend, $1,000 minimum); the Traditional 17 Month Fixed Jumbo Special is 4.20% APY ($100,000 minimum). Effective 09/01/2026.
note: Paraphrase of dep-09 (Traditional = Roth for the 17-month specials). S05 rates-59a9e6.md / personal-retirement-e090f4.md. Older snapshots: 3.85% (S03), 3.95% (S04).

question: What's the current 10-month certificate special? Not the jumbo one, the regular one.
expected_answer: The 10 Month Fixed Certificate Special pays 3.90% APY (3.86% dividend rate) with a $1,000 minimum, effective 09/01/2026. (The 10-month jumbo special is 4.00% APY with $100,000 minimum.)
note: S05 rates-59a9e6.md Special Certificates: 10M 3.86%/3.90%, 10M jumbo 3.96%/4.00% eff 09/01/2026. S01-S04 had 10M regular 3.76%/3.80% and jumbo 3.86%/3.90% - so 3.90% was formerly the jumbo rate; old regular rate 3.80% is the stale trap.

question: What's the rate on the Achieve Money Market right now?
expected_answer: New Achieve Money Market accounts opened with $25,000+ in new money (or matured Dupaco certificate funds) earn an introductory 4.00% dividend rate / 3.66% APY for the first 6 months (180 days); after that they earn 3.20% dividend / 3.25% APY. Balances under $25,000 earn 0.00%.
note: S05 earn-more-3ae90d.md (rate table, intro structure 'as of 8/24/26') and personal-savings-account-7ef72e.md banner. S05 /rates does NOT list Achieve. membermoneymarket-lp in S05 is a stale fetch (2026-06-15) showing only 3.20%/3.25% APY eff 10/01/2025 with no intro. Product page newer and > landing page. 3.25% is still valid as the post-promo rate, so not in must_not.

question: If I bring $25k of new money to Dupaco, what promo rate can I get on a money market?
expected_answer: The Achieve Money Market: introductory 4.00% dividend rate, 3.66% APY for the first six months on $25,000+ of new money (or matured Dupaco certificate funds), then a variable 3.20% dividend / 3.25% APY. One per member; business accounts excluded.
note: Paraphrase of dep-12. S05 earn-more-3ae90d.md. newmembermoneymarket-lp and makethemost-lp are expired in S05; membermoneymarket-lp (stale fetch 2026-06-15) shows 3.25% only.

question: What APY did the Achieve Money Market pay as of mid-July 2026?
expected_answer: 3.25% APY (3.20% dividend rate) on balances of $25,000-$1,000,000, with $25,000 of new money required to open (rates effective 10/01/2025). There was no introductory rate yet.
note: Ground truth = S03 (2026-06-09): membermoneymarket-lp, newmembermoneymarket-lp (3.20%/3.25%, eff 10/01/2025) and makethemost-lp ('3.25% APY on balances of $25,000 or more'). S03 /rates and savings page do not list Achieve. The 4.00%/3.66% intro first appears in S04 ('As of, 8/24/26').

question: if i put 20k in the achieve money market what would i earn
expected_answer: Nothing at that balance: Achieve requires $25,000 in new money to open, and the $0.01-$24,999.99 tier earns 0.00%. At $25,000+ you'd get the intro 4.00% dividend / 3.66% APY for 6 months, then 3.25% APY.
note: S05 earn-more-3ae90d.md tier table: $0.01-$24,999.99 0.00%/0.00%, min to open and min to earn $25,000. A sloppy answer just quotes 3.66% or 3.25%.

question: What money market accounts does Dupaco have?
expected_answer: Three: Investor's Choice Money Market ($2,500 to open; 0.20%-0.40% APY by tier), Achieve Money Market ($25,000 new money; intro 4.00% dividend/3.66% APY for 6 months, then 3.25% APY) and High-Yield Savings ($50,000 to open and maintain; 1.50%-2.45% APY). No check-writing; $250 minimum withdrawal.
note: S05 personal-savings-account-7ef72e.md: 'We offer three options-Investor's Choice, Achieve and High-Yield Savings'. In S01-S03 the same page said 'two options-Investor's Choice and High-Yield Savings', so an answer built on old snapshots omits Achieve.

question: what CD terms do you guys offer?
expected_answer: Regular term-share certificates: 6, 12, 18, 24, 30, 36, 48 and 60 months ($1,000 minimum). Specials: 10-month and 17-month fixed (regular $1,000 minimum, jumbo $100,000 minimum).
note: S05 rates-59a9e6.md Regular Certificates (8 terms) + Special Certificates (10M, 17M, each regular/jumbo). The certificate calculator page also lists 7 and 19 months, which are not offered terms. 25-month special existed only in S01/S02.

question: What kinds of IRAs can I open at Dupaco?
expected_answer: Traditional IRA, Roth IRA and SEP (Simplified Employee Pension) IRA, with fixed-rate (certificate), variable-rate or brokerage options. Dupaco also has the Launchpad Savings account as a starter (not an IRA).
note: S05 personal-retirement-e090f4.md sections: Traditional IRA, Roth IRA, Simplified Employee Pension ('Choose from fixed-rate, variable-rate or brokerage account options'). /rates lists Special, Regular and Variable IRA rates for Roth and Traditional.

question: whats the shortest term IRA certificate I can get? a blog said 18 months
expected_answer: 10 months: the Roth and Traditional 10 Month Fixed IRA Specials ($1,000 minimum; jumbo $100,000). There is also a 17-month IRA special. Regular IRA certificates are 18, 36 and 60 months, which is what the blog's '18 to 60 months' refers to.
note: S05 rates-59a9e6.md Special IRAs (10M and 17M) + Regular IRAs (18/36/60). Conflicting: learn-blog-knock-knock-ira-certificates (Oct 14, 2025) says 'choose a certificate IRA term from 18 to 60 months'. Rates page beats blog.

question: What's the APY on the 10 month jumbo special for a traditional IRA?
expected_answer: 3.90% APY (3.86% dividend rate), $100,000 minimum. Note this differs from the Roth 10-month jumbo special, which pays 4.00% APY (3.96%), and the regular (non-IRA) 10-month jumbo certificate at 4.00%.
note: S05 rates-59a9e6.md and personal-retirement-e090f4.md both list 'Traditional: 10 Month Fixed Jumbo Special | 3.86% | 3.90%' vs 'Roth: 10 Month Fixed Jumbo Special | 3.96% | 4.00%' (eff 09/01/2026). A system that assumes Roth = Traditional = certificate will wrongly say 4.00%. 4.00 not in must_not because a complete answer may contrast it.

question: Can my LLC open a Bright Savings account to get the 2.25%?
expected_answer: No. Bright Savings is available exclusively to consumer members; business, fiduciary, minor, estate and trust accounts are not eligible (it must be opened online, one per SSN). A business could use Business High-Yield Savings (1.50%-2.45% APY, $50,000 minimum) or Investor's Choice instead.
note: S05 rates-59a9e6.md and savings-account-online-savings-account-8ad278.md Bright Savings fine print: 'available exclusively to consumer members. Business, fiduciary, minor, estate, and trust accounts are not eligible.' business-rates lists no Bright Savings.

question: What dividend rate does an HSA earn with about $12,000 in it?
expected_answer: 0.30% (dividend rate and APY) for the $10,000-$24,999.99 Health Savings Account tier, effective 06/02/2026.
note: S05 rates-59a9e6.md HSA: $25k+ 0.35%, $10k-$24,999.99 0.30%, $2,500-$9,999.99 0.25%, $0.01-$2,499.99 0.20%. 0.15% is the same balance tier for Share Savings (entity confusion). HSA rates unchanged across snapshots (older pages show eff 01/06/2026).

question: What does the Launchpad savings account pay and what's the catch?
expected_answer: Launchpad Savings pays 3.25% APY (3.21% dividend) on balances from $5 up to $1,000. Open with $5; if no deposit in any 90-day period the account is closed; once it reaches $1,000 you have 90 days to move the funds into a Dupaco Financial Services IRA or it's closed (less a $5 fee) into share savings; $5 penalty per withdrawal; it is not a retirement account and has no tax benefits.
note: S05 rates-59a9e6.md (Launchpad table eff 06/02/2026, new on /rates in S05) and personal-retirement-e090f4.md (same 3.21%/3.25%, labeled eff 01/06/2026). Same rate, different effective dates.

question: what do i have to do to get the $300 for opening a checking account?
expected_answer: Open a new Dupaco checking account using promo code CHECK300 (or mention the offer in branch/by phone), make at least $500 of acceptable deposits (cash, checks, ACH, wires; not internal transfers) within 90 days, and meet the Active Checking definition within 90 days (direct deposit plus 5 check/debit/ACH transactions, or 10 checks / 8 debit / 5 ACH / 3 bill pays). The $300 is deposited within 5 business days of completing the requirements.
note: S05 checking-offer-lp-a3545a.md and tax-checking-offer-lp-224250.md fine print. The 'Make the Most' bundle page (makethemost-lp) is expired in S04/S05. Older S01/S02 fine print said payout '3-5 business days later'.

question: I closed my Dupaco checking about a year ago. If I open a new one now can I still get the $300 CHECK300 bonus?
expected_answer: No. Members are ineligible if they open a Dupaco Share Draft Checking account within 730 days of closing one they owned, so closing it a year ago disqualifies you.
note: S05 checking-offer-lp-a3545a.md / tax-checking-offer-lp-224250.md eligibility: 'within 730 days of closing'. S01/S02 checking-offer-lp and makethemost-lp said 'within 180 days after closing' - under the old rule a 1-year gap would qualify. Changed in S03.

question: how long do i have to wait after closing my old dupaco checking before i qualify for the new checking $300 offer
expected_answer: 730 days (about two years) after closing your previous Dupaco Share Draft Checking account; existing checking owners are also ineligible.
note: Paraphrase of dep-25. S05 checking-offer-lp-a3545a.md. Old S01/S02 versions: 180 days.

question: Back in May 2026 (say May 20), how long after closing a Dupaco checking account did you have to wait to qualify for the $300 checking offer?
expected_answer: 180 days: members were ineligible if they opened a new consumer checking account within 180 days after closing a prior one. The $300 was paid 3-5 business days after meeting the requirements ($500 deposits within 90 days plus Active Checking).
note: Ground truth = S02 (2026-05-19) checking-offer-lp-a3545a.md: 'ineligible for this offer if opening a consumer share draft checking account within 180 days after closing'. S03+ changed to 730 days.

question: What's your 7 month CD rate?
expected_answer: Dupaco doesn't publish a 7-month certificate rate - the offered terms are 6, 12, 18, 24, 30, 36, 48 and 60 months plus 10- and 17-month specials. (The certificate calculator lists 7 months as an input option but no rate.)
note: No '7 Month' certificate in any snapshot's rates/savings/business pages (only '17 Month' matches). calculators-certificate-calculator-d9cb5a.md offers 7 and 19 month terms in a dropdown with no rate. Should decline to give a rate (may point to existing terms).

question: what's the rate on a 7-month term share certificate? your calculator has 7 months as an option
expected_answer: There is no published 7-month term-share certificate rate; the calculator's term list is just an input. Published terms are 6-60 months regular plus 10- and 17-month specials.
note: Paraphrase of dep-28. Calculator page lists 7/19 months, rates pages do not.

question: What APY does Business Analysis Checking earn?
expected_answer: Dupaco doesn't publish a dividend rate/APY for Business Analysis Checking; only Business 1st Rate Checking has a rate table. Analysis Checking is fee-based (monthly fees can be offset by balances); contact Business Services for details.
note: S05 business-checking-accounts-d230fa.md and business-rates-7b3f99.md: rate table only for Business 1st Rate Checking. Fee schedule PDF lists Analysis checking $10/month and per-item fees but no rate. A system might wrongly reuse the 2.50% Business 1st Rate figure.

question: What's the business 1st Rate Checking APY?
expected_answer: Business 1st Rate Checking pays 2.50% APY (2.47% dividend) on balances of $5,000-$24,999.99; 0.10% on $25,000+; 0.00% under $5,000 (effective 06/02/2026). A $10 monthly fee applies unless the monthly balance stays above $5,000.
note: S05 business-rates-7b3f99.md and business-checking-accounts-d230fa.md (eff 06/02/2026). S01/S02 business-rates said 'Earn up to 3.00% APY' with 2.96%/3.00% tier (eff 07/01/2025).

question: when does holiday club pay out and what rate does it earn?
expected_answer: On Oct. 31 the Holiday Club balance automatically transfers to your checking account. It earns 0.20% APY (0.20% dividend) on balances of $0.01+, with no minimum balance; early withdrawals close the account, and it renews automatically each year.
note: S05 personal-savings-account-7ef72e.md Holiday Club section and rates-59a9e6.md (0.20%/0.20%, eff 06/02/2026). Newsroom releases give 2024/2025 savings totals, not rates.
